parameter: Malignant brain & CNS tumours per year (India)
source: IARC GLOBOCAN, India, estimates for 2024 (gco.iarc.who.int/today), accessed 27 Oct 2026
note: Malignant only; held constant across scenarios

parameter: Glioma share of malignant CNS tumours
source: Kumar et al., Cureus 2026 (Jaipur, n=1315): (398 astrocytomas x (1-0.1746 grade I) + 92 oligodendrogliomas) / 745 malignant = 56%
note: Hospital series; base is derived by us, low/high are scenario bounds

parameter: Grade 2 diffuse glioma share of all gliomas
source: Base: Thambi et al., JCDR 2017 (n=510): grade 2 diffuse astrocytoma = 26.9% of glial tumours. High: Kaur et al., Neurol India 2025: 49/115 = 42.6% of adult-type diffuse gliomas (excludes non-diffuse types). Low: scenario
note: Series differ in case mix; this step is one of the largest sources of uncertainty

parameter: IDH-mutant share of grade 2 diffuse glioma
source: Kaur et al., Neurol India 2025: grade 2 astrocytoma 30/41 = 73.2%, grade 2 oligodendroglioma 8/8; pooled 38/49 = 77.6% (derived). High 0.90 is a scenario inside the 73.6-100% range Kaur cites for other Indian studies

parameter: Share of patients who get IDH testing
source: No Indian national testing rate is published. ISNO consensus (Santosh et al., Neurol India 2019) describes an IHC-first approach and states molecular tests are not always affordable
note: Pure assumption; see centre evidence map: only 4 of 37 listed centres publicly confirm both neurosurgery and molecular pathology

parameter: Share of IDH-mutant tumours detected by the testing pathway
source: Kaur et al.: IDH1 R132H IHC sensitivity 84%. High = reflex sequencing/PCR for IHC-negative cases (ISNO approach)
note: IHC misses non-R132H variants and IDH2

parameter: Share meeting INDIGO-type eligibility (post-surgery, untreated, measurable non-enhancing disease, KPS>=80)
source: Criteria from Mellinghoff et al., NEJM 2023 (INDIGO). The share meeting them in India is not published
note: Pure assumption; the INDIGO label may be broader or narrower than trial criteria

evidence_type: Scenario anchored on a trial result
source: INDIGO median PFS 27.7 months (Mellinghoff et al., NEJM 2023) used as a proxy for time on therapy
note: PFS is not time on treatment; real persistence is unknown
